info.title: Canaveral consumer lease API
info.description: Implemented controller consumer subset. Independently usable execution; ordinary runners remain gated for consumer lease execution. No administrator, enrollment, model, registry or host API is implied. POST bodies are JSON objects of at most 1 MiB with a single Content-Length. Browser Origin requests are rejected. Remote use requires HTTPS; the embedded server uses HTTP behind operator TLS termination. Credentials are opaque bearer secrets, never URL parameters.

get.description: HTTP handshake only. Requires Upgrade: websocket, Connection: Upgrade, Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13, a valid WebSocket key and Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: canaveral-session-v1. No Origin, body, credentials in URLs or query fields. Exactly one current consumer peer may attach. The worker connects outbound separately; readiness requires both peers. Frame/control/RFB contracts are documented separately. No automatic replay after disconnect.

201.description: New durable intent created; replay returns 200

post.description: Requires the current lease key and a ready eligible member. Persist the request UUID and inspect it after an unconfirmed response. Identical replay returns the current receipt and never issues a second effect. Dispatch without a completed receipt becomes unknown when authorization ends. A queued command has a 120-second start deadline bounded by lease expiry; renewals do not restart it. At most 32 pending discrete commands per host; streaming files and PTYs have separate contracts.

ApplicationBearer.description: Operator-created application identity, limited to its pinned catalogue and owned lifecycle.

LeaseBearer.description: Current scoped key for exactly one lease; expiry, revocation, readiness and session generation still apply.

ttlSeconds.description: Linux leases require at least 30 seconds (400 linux_ttl_below_minimum otherwise); acquisition also refuses a configured default or maximum below 30 seconds, without clamping. Other lease kinds retain their existing bounds.

credential.description: Returned only by explicit lease-key rotation. Store privately; never log this response.

ttlSeconds.description: Linux leases require at least 30 seconds (400 linux_ttl_below_minimum otherwise); acquisition also refuses a configured default or maximum below 30 seconds, without clamping. Other lease kinds retain their existing bounds.

MutationResult.description: A replay returns the original mutation result and a fresh lease view; their revisions and states may differ.

Error.description: Normal errors carry correlation and retry fields; unexpected service failures retain the legacy error-only 503 response.

CreateOperation.description: Durable common guest operation with a caller-owned UUID. Native capability and argument validation also apply. App/installer management is not part of this subset.

data.description: Runtime decoding enforces 512 KiB. Use upload sessions for unbounded total file size.

source.description: Opaque source context, at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes; no behavior.
